newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya 91-day bills bids accepted at 21.604 pct.
newsitem.headline: Kenya 91-day bills bids accepted at 21.604 pct.

text.p: Kenya's central bank accepted bids on its 91-day main category of treasury bills at 21.604 percent at its weekly auction on Thursday, versus a previous 21.609 percent, officials said.
On the 28-day category it accepted bids at 16.500 percent from 16.314 percent.
Out of a total of 4.857 billion shillings worth of bids tendered, the bank accepted 3.265 billion shillings.

In the 28-day category of bills, the bank accepted all 16.70 million shillings tendered while on the 91-day category it accepted 3.248 billion shillings out of a total of 4.841 billion shillings tendered.
There were no tenders for 182-day category.
In a circular issued last week on Tuesday, the central bank said bills issued from January 1 would be in book-entry form.
"This means that no paper certificates will be issued except where special circumstances surrounding an investor warrant the issuing of such certificates," it said.
The bank invited tenders for bills worth eight billion shillings for the auction on Thursday next week. ($1=55 shillings)
